upstream: hexstrike-ai (0x4m4), pinned d689933 — vendored NON-runnable; 79 distinct external tools
note: fact_capable is set ONLY when a runner-owned oracle re-drive exists AND the ToolSpec passes the conformance battery (live.conformance). Everything else is LEAD-only or excluded. The count that matters is fact_capable, not the upstream tool count. Two FACT families are VIGIL-DIRECT (no tool is the authority): VERSION_RANGE via live.sbom (SBOM/dependency-CVE) and ACHIEVED_STATE via live.web_redrive — both HEADER-DERIVED (3xx Location, CORS headers, OIDC via Location) and BODY-DERIVED evidence. Body-derived branches are FACT-capable: the capture reverses Content-Encoding and determines the charset the way a browser does (integration/vigil_integration/live/body_decode.py — complete single-member gzip/deflate + the WHATWG encoding map), and the JS-redirect branch mints only from executable code, decided by a real tokenizer (engine/crucible/framework/v2/scanner/js_lex.py:sink_is_executable), not a regex. They remain NOT CLEAN-capable, for a different reason than the decode: a non-firing cannot distinguish 'the document declares no redirect' from 'we could not read the document', and lexing cannot prove a runtime-assembled sink absent. An undeclared charset, brotli/zstd, concatenated members and truncated reads are INCONCLUSIVE, and no-channel is INCONCLUSIVE not CLEAN. Their proposer tools (trivy/grype, httpx) keep fact_capable=false by design.

tools.notes: runner re-drives its own gated TLS handshake; weak_tls + weak_crypto_artifact FACTs. weak_tls is scoped to what a modern client still negotiates (honest).

tools.name: httpx
tools.notes: HTTP exposure is re-derived by VIGIL's live.web_redrive ACHIEVED_STATE path (no install): VIGIL issues its OWN gated, no-redirect capture and the deterministic predicate_oracle adjudicates — the tool is only a URL proposer, never the fact authority (fact_capable stays false). CAPABILITY BOUNDARY (honest, narrower than the family name): HEADER-DERIVED evidence — a 3xx Location host, CORS reflected-origin-with-credentials, an OIDC redirect proven through Location — is both FACT- and CLEAN-capable. BODY-DERIVED branches (meta-refresh / body redirect, host-header reflected into HTML, the JS redirect sink) are FACT-capable but NOT CLEAN-capable. The decode gap that once made them unsound is CLOSED: integration/vigil_integration/live/body_decode.py reverses Content-Encoding (a complete, single-member, bounded gzip/deflate stream) and determines the charset the way a browser does (BOM, then the transport Content-Type label resolved through the WHATWG encoding map, strict decode), and body_semantically_available gates every body-dependent predicate — so an undeclared charset, a brotli/zstd body, concatenated members or a truncated read yield INCONCLUSIVE instead of a CLEAN over a document VIGIL never read. The JS-redirect branch mints only from EXECUTABLE code, decided by a real tokenizer (engine/crucible/framework/v2/scanner/js_lex.py:sink_is_executable — comments, string/template literals and ambiguous /-spans are excluded structurally), so it is FACT-capable rather than LEAD-only. What keeps the body branches from CLEAN is no longer decoding but ABSENCE: a non-firing cannot distinguish 'the document declares no redirect' from 'we could not read this document', and lexing cannot prove a runtime-assembled sink absent (that needs DOM rendering, which is not wired). Per-branch limitations and blocking_work are in docs/capability-matrix/evidence-branches.json, which governs admission.
